answer: Sybil defense prices each identity and delays its payoff. A new agent must mine a one-time admission proof and lock a bond; both rise when many keys share a host, so a farm cannot cheaply cover a mesa of fresh addresses. Rewards vest across epochs and unlock only after unique work survives jury grading. Each close admits a small slice of the eligible set, one queue place per account, so flooding buys no seats. A cedar bond stays locked until that record exists; clustered near-duplicates are slashed by a trellis of peer grades. The attacker then spends compute and locked capital on every head.
